scope: Focused review of all 280 active stems for redundant wording and explicit answer cues

independent_review.finding: Final stems, every option, and rationales retain one best answer in the ordinary textbook context. Neither updated rationale relies on deleted wording. Difficulty and coverage remain unchanged.

changes.stem_before: A firm paid a nonrefundable €6,000 deposit. Completing the project now costs €2,000 and yields a certain €3,000 benefit; cancellation yields nothing further. Ignoring other effects, what should it do?
changes.stem_after: A firm paid a nonrefundable €6,000 deposit. Completing the project now costs €2,000 and yields a certain €3,000 benefit; cancellation yields nothing further. Which choice maximizes its remaining net benefit?

changes.stem_before: Researchers want to estimate the effect of an encouraging label on task performance. Which comparison is strongest, assuming random assignment is feasible?
changes.stem_after: Researchers want to estimate the effect of an encouraging label on task performance. Which comparison is strongest?

changes.stem_before: A team thinks a service succeeds only when response time is under one hour. Which observation would most directly challenge that necessity claim?
changes.stem_after: A team thinks a service succeeds only when response time is under one hour. Which observation would most directly challenge that claim?

changes.stem_before: A form changes “10% service failures” to “90% service success,” while leaving the preselected option unchanged. Which feature was directly changed?
changes.stem_after: A form changes “10% service failures” to “90% service success.” Which feature was directly changed?

explanation_changes.before: The stem holds the preselection fixed.
explanation_changes.after: Changing this wording does not select a different option.

changes.stem_before: A fair coin has landed heads four times. Tosses are independent. What is the probability of heads on the next toss?
changes.stem_after: A fair coin has landed heads four times. What is the probability of heads on the next toss?

explanation_changes.before: Independence leaves the next-toss probability unchanged.
explanation_changes.after: In the usual fair-coin model, tosses are independent, so the previous heads do not change the next-toss probability of 1/2.

changes.stem_before: Every application has a final outcome recorded as either success or failure. A report says 3% fail. Its complementary frame must describe the same applications and period. Which statement qualifies?
changes.stem_after: Every application has a final outcome recorded as either success or failure. A report says 3% fail. Which statement gives the complementary frame?

changes.stem_before: Ignoring tax and contractual restrictions, €100 from a refund buys the same goods as €100 from wages. Which benchmark does this illustrate?
changes.stem_after: €100 from a refund buys the same goods as €100 from wages. Which benchmark does this illustrate?

changes.stem_before: An investment independently multiplies wealth by 1.5 or 0.6 with equal probability each period. A sample contains one of each outcome. Which statement correctly compares expected one-period return with the realized two-period path?
changes.stem_after: An investment multiplies wealth by 1.5 or 0.6 with equal probability each period. A sample contains one of each outcome. Which statement correctly compares expected one-period return with the realized two-period path?

changes.stem_before: A tenant says, “The rent must be €900.” The underlying concern is having predictable housing costs while studying. Which is the position, and which is the interest?
changes.stem_after: A tenant says, “The rent must be €900.” She wants predictable housing costs while studying. Which is the position, and which is the interest?

changes.stem_before: A buyer will pay at most €120 and a seller will accept at least €90. Price is the only issue and both limits include all relevant costs. What is the zone of possible agreement?
changes.stem_after: A buyer will pay at most €120 and a seller will accept at least €90. What is the price range of possible agreement?

changes.stem_before: Feasible packages give utility pairs (buyer, seller): A=(6,6), B=(8,7), C=(9,5), D=(5,9). More utility is preferred. Which package is Pareto dominated within this set?
changes.stem_after: Feasible packages give utility pairs (buyer, seller): A=(6,6), B=(8,7), C=(9,5), D=(5,9). Which package is Pareto dominated within this set?
